newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ING DETAILS HIDDEN RESERVES TREATMENT.
newsitem.headline: ING DETAILS HIDDEN RESERVES TREATMENT.

text.p: Bank-insurer ING Groep said on Wednesday it planned to transfer about half its hidden reserves to a fund for general banking risks (FAR) and the other half to a general reserve, without disclosing the total amount.

"We announce our hidden reserves on April 3, 1997, together with the announcement of our 1996 results," board member Cees Maas told a news conference, during which he unveiled more details on the intended bourse listing in New York.
Last month ABN AMRO said its hidden reserves were 4.02 billion guilders at December 31, 1996 and unlisted Rabobank said its hidden reserves amounted to 3.5 billion guilders.
Dutch banks have been ordered to unveil their hidden reserve by the year 2000 to comply with changes to European Union rules.
Maas said ING also had to unveil more financial details ahead of its listing in the U.S.
ING said in a presentation that it would offer "more openness regarding ING Group figures" ahead of the U.S. listing.
ING said earlier today it was planning to list its shares in New York in June this year.
